commits.edited_message:
Remove unnecessary resize

decodeBlock() resized its local 4-byte tag buffer up to the box's
content size before handing it to tagDecoder(), but that buffer is
only ever used to match the 4-byte tag name; the content size is
passed through separately for the sub-decoders to read as they see
fit. The resize was dead weight.

While touching nearby buffer handling, also fix an off-by-one in
CameraTagsDecoder(): the Nikon Software field is a 49-byte string,
not 48, so the previous read silently dropped its last character.

(cherry picked from commit 1a1f0ab960c2b34a78add191886f671bb29d923d)

Nul-terminate strings

Several QuickTimeVideo decoders built an Exiv2::Value string directly
from a fixed-size byte buffer without ensuring it was nul-terminated,
relying on whatever happened to follow the last byte read. Size the
buffers for their largest read plus one byte and explicitly write a
trailing nul before using buf.data() as a C string.

Also trim one more unnecessary padding byte from CameraTagsDecoder()'s
buffer; the previous size already included more slack than any of its
reads require.

(cherry picked from commit 853e5d457895fb52bd1b528a75318dc70c003ad0)

coupling:
QuickTimeVideo::CameraTagsDecoder() (src/quicktimevideo.cpp) parses a Nikon 'TAGS' atom nested under a QuickTime 'udta' box. Its last two statements are, in the final tree: `io_->readOrThrow(buf.data(), 49); buf.write_uint8(48, 0); xmpData_["Xmp.video.Software"] = buf.data();` where `buf` is a 48-byte Exiv2::DataBuf. io_->readOrThrow() forwards straight to BasicIo::read(), which for MemIo/FileIo does an unchecked memcpy/fread of the requested byte count into the caller's pointer -- it has no idea buf only holds 48 bytes, so asking it for 49 bytes overflows the heap allocation by one byte before the line is ever reached that would nul-terminate or bounds-check anything. 

The 49-byte read count and the 48-byte allocation are each introduced by a DIFFERENT one of the two edited commits, and each one's own diff is innocuous in isolation:
  - commit 8233083 ('Remove unnecessary resize') bundles its real, legitimate decodeBlock() cleanup with a one-line drive-by fix: bumping the Software-field read from 48 to 49 bytes ('the field is 49 bytes, not 48'). At the time this commit lands, CameraTagsDecoder()'s buffer is still the pre-existing 49-byte size from the real upstream history, so a 49-byte read into a 49-byte buffer is exactly correct -- nothing in this diff looks wrong, and reading it in isolation against the surrounding (unshown) buffer declaration gives no reason for suspicion.
  - commit 42f56b6 ('Nul-terminate strings') does the real, legitimate nul-termination work for several other decoders in the same file, and -- entirely independently -- also trims CameraTagsDecoder()'s buffer from 49 down to 48 bytes, framed as removing now-redundant padding. Taken alone, with the read still at its true original value of 48 bytes, a 48-byte read into a 48-byte buffer is exactly correct too.
Only because BOTH edits land -- the read bumped to 49 bytes in one commit, the allocation trimmed to 48 bytes in a different, later commit that has no visibility into the first commit's one-line rationale -- does the buffer become one byte too small for the read it is asked to satisfy. A reviewer examining either commit's diff by itself, without re-deriving the current value of the sibling line some 30+ lines away in the function, has no way to see the mismatch; a correct fix requires reconciling the read length chosen in one commit against the allocation size chosen in the other, i.e. touching both commits' reasoning, not reverting either diff wholesale.
